verdict.rationale: Viam documents a simulated machine environment: the setup wizard can run a machine in the cloud before hardware arrives, Viam 101 builds a cell in simulation, and the RDK ships a fake/dummy config. It also documents hardware-agnostic component APIs, so changing a camera or motor in config keeps code working without a rewrite. Together these strongly imply sim-to-real code portability, but the evidence never explicitly describes moving the same program from a simulated machine to a real one by swapping config. missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of a sim-to-real workflow with unchanged code, detail on simulation fidelity and which components can be simulated, independent or hands-on corroboration.
